key_insight: UniX unifies autoregressive semantic modeling and diffusion-based pixel synthesis in a single chest X‑ray foundation model by separating task-specific pathways to avoid the usual trade-off between understanding and generation.
problem_solved: Existing unified medical models compromise either semantic understanding or pixel-level generation because shared-parameter autoregressive designs force conflicting representations; UniX addresses this by decoupling and coordinating both goals.
method: Hybrid architecture: shared encoder/latent space with two specialized decoders—an autoregressive head for semantic/reporting tasks and a diffusion head for high-fidelity image generation.
Task-aware training: joint optimization with separate objectives and conditioning so each pathway preserves its inductive bias while benefiting from shared representation learning.
Cross-path coordination: lightweight adapters/conditioning modules enable information flow between heads to align semantics and pixels without parameter interference.
impact: UniX enables a single, deployable medical foundation model that performs both diagnosis-oriented understanding and realistic X‑ray generation well, improving downstream efficiency, data augmentation, and clinical utility for AI/ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: shared encoder with split autoregressive and diffusion decoders, showing data flow and conditioning.
Performance comparison chart: bars or radar showing understanding vs generation metrics for UniX vs parameter-shared and task-specific baselines.
Qualitative examples: paired columns of generated chest X‑rays and corresponding diagnostic reports to illustrate joint capability.
Training flowchart: joint-loss schematic highlighting separate objectives and cross-path adapters/conditioning.
paper_title: UniX: Unifying Autoregression and Diffusion for Chest X-Ray Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ruiheng Zhang, Jingfeng Yao, Huangxuan Zhao, Hao Yan, Xiao He
